items.reply: This is by design: the spec puts --shout before the name, and other argument orders are out of scope. `greet.sh ada --shout` prints `hello ada`, the same as before the change.

finding.proof: bin/greet.sh:9 runs `echo "${line}"` on a name taken from argv. Under macOS /bin/sh, `sh bin/greet.sh 'a\tb'` prints a real tab; before the change printf printed a backslash and a t.
finding.claim: `echo` expands backslash sequences in the name on some POSIX sh builds, so output without --shout changes for such names, against the spec's 'without --shout nothing changes'.

items.note: True: `tr a-z A-Z` (now bin/greet.sh:8) uppercases ASCII only, and its ranges are unspecified outside the C locale. The author limits names to ASCII and the spec asks no more; `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'` is the portable form if that changes.

items.reply: POSIX sh has no boolean type, so a string flag is the usual form. The script also shifts --shout off at line 5 before reading the name, so by line 8 there is no argument left to test; holding the result in `shout` is what keeps that working.
Checked: `sh bin/greet.sh --shout` with no name prints `HELLO WORLD`, as the author said.

finding.claim: No test covers --shout: tests/greet_test.sh only checks the plain greeting, so neither `--shout` alone (HELLO WORLD) nor the spec's `--shout ada` (HELLO ADA) is guarded.
finding.suggestion: Add checks to tests/greet_test.sh that `greet.sh --shout` prints `HELLO WORLD` and `greet.sh --shout ada` prints `HELLO ADA`.

noticed.text: The author said in thread d-reply they would switch to printf, but the commit under review (add0601) still ends in `echo`; nothing has changed since the earlier judgment.
The MR's only commit message is `Add --shout` and has no typo; the resolved typo thread matches nothing in the commit as it is now.
